issue_context.title: ENH: Return type of pandas.DataFrame.dropna is incorrectly None
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [x] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

example = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2, 3], 'b': [4, np.nan, 6]})
example.dropna()
```


#### Problem description

Currently, the return type of `pandas.DataFrame.dropna` is missing. The documentation correctly states that the return type should be `Optional[DataFrame]`, but the function definition lacks a return type, so type checkers (in my case pyright) incorrectly throw the type as `None`.

The issue occurs in the source code here:
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/3e89b4c4b1580aa890023fc550774e63d499da25/pandas/core/frame.py#L5041

It should be typed as seen in `pandas.DataFrame.drop_duplicates`, seen below:
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/3e89b4c4b1580aa890023fc550774e63d499da25/pandas/core/frame.py#L5183-L5189

More broadly, it seems that the `dropna` function is missing typing for its arguments as well.

#### Expected Output

The return type of `pandas.DataFrame.dropna` should be `Optional[DataFrame]`

I don't think this should be too hard to fix. I'll work in it tonight and submit a PR in the next day or two.

comments: Hi @rbpatt2019, thanks for the report! Typing PR's are certainly welcome - it's not that `dropna` is missing typing accidentally, it just hasn't been typed yet (same for many places in the codebase).

Thanks @rbpatt2019 for the report. We can close this as we have mypy strictness flags and reports (an also now pyright #39813) to monitor type completeness rather than having open issues on the tracker.

review_comments:
we now have an `IndexLabel` alias in pandas._typing that could be used for subset.

```suggestion
        subset: Optional[IndexLabel] = ...,
```

I see you used #37137 as a example. However the motivation for that PR was to remove an `assert df is not None` from the codebase and the return type of `Optional[DataFrame]` not touched.

Not needed to be done in this PR, but just FYI if the motivation for adding the types is for the public api, then the return type should be the same type as self for subclassed DataFrames.
I'm pretty sure this comment has to go above the decorator?

It doesn't in `pandas.core.frame.reset_index`, which doesn't seem to cause any problems. Also, it passed the typing portion of CI/Checks build, so I think we are fine. Happy to move it if there is a style preference though!
I don't have a preference since it passes CI
